public_rationale: Marcus forecast that AI agents would not do a huge fraction of human knowledge work in 2025, 2026 or 2027, except in narrow use cases. The window ends on 31 December 2027, after the evaluation date. Under the contract, the forecast cannot be supported before then. A benchmark paper from 30 October 2025 found that the best agent automated 2.5% of the real-world projects in its Remote Labor Index. That is a benchmark result. It is not a measure of the share of knowledge work agents actually did across the economy. The packet has no such economy-wide measure. So the early-contradiction rule, which needs credible measurement of agents doing a large share of knowledge work broadly, is not met.
limitations: The packet has no economy-wide measure of the share of knowledge work done by agents.
Benchmark results are not the same as real-world deployment data.
'Huge fraction' and 'narrow use cases' have no defined thresholds.
A McKinsey survey on agent adoption could not be loaded and was not used.

criteria.support_condition: Through the end of 2027, labor and adoption data show that agents do only a small share of knowledge work overall, beyond narrow uses such as coding or customer service.
criteria.contradiction_condition: Credible data show that, at some point in 2025–2027, agents did a large share of knowledge work broadly, not just in narrow niches.
